In order to make it appear as if my bank was actually guilty of crimes for which no one associated with the bank was ever charged, Google writes, "While the tax probe did not file criminal charges directly against Schiff, multiple bank customers were audited or arrested."

First of all, the bank probe did not result in charges filed against anyone, not just me. Google implies that charges may have been filed, just not directly against me. It leaves open the false impression that there may have been indirect charges filed against me.

Google then goes out of its way to points out that "multiple bank customers were audited" to imply that despite the absence of charges against me personally, the bank was guilty, otherwise there would not have been customer audits.. But audits are common, and being audited does not imply the subject of the audit did anything wrong. 

In fact, Google does not report the results of those audits, if they even occurred. Plus, wrongdoing on the part of customers does not imply wrongdoing on the part of the bank. Yet Google uses the audits to imply the bank did something wrong, despite the lack of criminal charges against me directly.

Google also mentions that multiple bank customers were arrested. I know of just two people who were arrested and were reported to have possibly been customers of my bank. I have no idea if they were, but there were no follow-up reports of any charges actually being filed, let alone criminal convictions. Yet Google cites this to imply guilt on the part of the bank, even though no actual evidence of guilt was ever found.
